name: Thymic Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Thymic Epithelial Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of anterior mediastinal mass on chest imaging (CT or MRI)
Histopathological confirmation of thymic epithelial tumor subtype
Association with paraneoplastic syndromes such as myasthenia gravis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiologic evidence of anterior mediastinal mass plus histopathological confirmation of thymic epithelial tumor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires tissue biopsy for definitive classification; imaging guides surgical planning.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior mediastinal mass detected on imaging
searchTerms: mass in front of chest detected by scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Myasthenia gravis with fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness
pathognomonic.notes: Occurs in approximately 30-50% of thymoma cases
searchTerms: weakness in skeletal muscles varying over time

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to anterior mediastinum
common.notes: Due to tumor invasion or compression
searchTerms: chest pain in front of chest

common.notes: From mass effect on lungs or airways

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

occasional.notes: Due to tumor invasion or inflammation

searchTerms: failure to produce red blood cells
pure red cell aplasia causing anemia
low antibody levels causing immune deficiency
immune system weakness from low antibodies

rare.symptomName: Superior phrenic nerve palsy causing diaphragmatic paralysis
searchTerms: phrenic nerve damage leading to breathing problems

laboratory: Elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies in myasthenia gravis
Anemia or pure red cell aplasia on complete blood count
imaging: CT scan showing anterior mediastinal mass with possible invasion
MRI for soft tissue characterization and local extent
Chest X-ray may show widened mediastinum
genetic: No specific germline mutations routinely identified
Somatic mutations in GTF2I gene reported in some thymomas
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratin and CD5 in thymic carcinoma

distinguishingFeatures: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

redFlags: Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
New onset or worsening myasthenic crisis
references: Travis WD et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. IARC, 2021.
Detterbeck FC et al. The Masaoka-Koga stage classification for thymic malignancies. J Thorac Oncol. 2011.
Marx A et al. The 2021 WHO classification of thymic epithelial tumors. Virchows Arch. 2021.
